explanation: In the 1150s BC, under Ramesses III, craftsmen from Deir el-Medina, near the Valley of the Kings, downed tools over late grain rations. A papyrus in Turin records it.

claims.text: In the 1150s BC, workers who built royal tombs in ancient Egypt went on strike when their rations were late.
In year 29 of Ramesses III, in the 1150s BC, the tomb workers of Deir el-Medina stopped work over late grain rations.
Deir el-Medina was the village of the workers who built the tombs in the Valley of the Kings.
The Turin Strike Papyrus records the protest.
